questions.q: What's the real distinction between a problem that's the customer's own responsibility to fix and one that's genuinely ServiceNow's responsibility?
options: Every slowdown is always ServiceNow's responsibility to fix, regardless of cause
There is no meaningful distinction between the two categories
A customization-caused problem (a recursive Business Rule, an unindexed custom table) is the customer's to fix; a genuine platform/infrastructure issue is ServiceNow's
Every slowdown is always the customer's responsibility, regardless of cause
questions.explain: Configuration the customer introduced is theirs to diagnose and fix with this course's own tools; platform/infrastructure problems sit on ServiceNow's side.

questions.q: Why does opening a support case with just "the instance feels slow" typically slow things down?
options: Support has no transaction, time window, or specifics to investigate, so the first reply is usually a request for exactly the evidence that should have been gathered up front
Support cases require no evidence of any kind to begin investigating
ServiceNow Support ignores all vague case submissions permanently
Vague reports are always resolved faster than detailed ones
questions.explain: A vague report burns a full round trip while Support asks for the specifics needed to even start, instead of beginning real investigation immediately.

questions.q: What kind of evidence actually moves a support case forward quickly, per this lesson?
options: A general statement that performance has felt worse lately
Specific Slow Request Log entries, exact timestamps, which users/features were affected, and what recently changed
A request that ServiceNow simply restart the instance with no further detail
A list of every user who has ever logged into the instance
questions.explain: Concrete, timestamped evidence lets ServiceNow's engineers start investigating the actual mechanism immediately.

questions.q: How does Lesson 19's triage sequence relate to opening a strong support case?
options: A well-triaged incident essentially writes its own support case, since the triage evidence is the same evidence a case needs
Triage should only happen after a support case is already closed
Support cases replace the need for any triage work beforehand
Triage and support cases are unrelated processes with no overlap
questions.explain: Scope confirmed via Instance Health, deployment timing checked, and resource usage checked are exactly the facts a strong case states up front.

questions.q: Why is gathering evidence before opening a case described as more than bureaucratic box-checking?
options: It is purely a formality with no actual effect on resolution speed
It's the single thing that determines whether the case resolves in one exchange or many
It guarantees the case will always be classified as a platform issue
ServiceNow charges extra for cases opened without evidence
questions.explain: Handing over concrete evidence up front lets engineers skip the exchange that would otherwise just be spent establishing what happened.
